# How to use Christ as the Truth,
### for the clarification of our State.

In such a case as this, there is ground for a poor soul to use **Christ** to find a way out; and a way out can be obtained in **God's** time, and when He deems it most fit, by making a right use of Him and going out to Him who is the **Truth**. Therefore, a soul who desires to have their state and condition cleared up—and who has had no discovery <note>discovery: in this context, a spiritual realization or "revelation" of one's standing with God</note> that they are reconciled with **God** through **Jesus** and are in a state of grace—should use **Christ** as the **Truth**; and to this end:

**Firstly**, look out toward **Christ** as toward a sympathetic **High Priest**, faithful and merciful, who, being made like us in all things except for sin, has compassion for and comes to the aid of those who are tempted, **Heb. 2: v. 17, 18.** and as a **Priest** who is touched with the feeling of our infirmities, **Heb. 4: v. 15.** Although **Christ** never, even in the deepest of His darkness, called His **Sonship** <note>Sonship: the status of being a child of God</note> into question, but acknowledged that **God** was His **God**, even when He was forsaken: **Psal. 22: verse 1. Math. 27: verse 46. Marc. 15: v. 34.** nevertheless, He knew what it was to be tempted to call His **Sonship** into question, as when the **Devil** said to Him, **Math. 4: v... If you are the Son of God.** And He knows what such misery—just as He was in, wrestling with an angry **God** <note>original: "toornige Godt." This refers to the theological belief that on the cross, Christ bore the weight of divine judgment against sin.</note> who hid Himself and forsook Him—will work in a poor **Sinner**. And being a merciful and compassionate **High Priest**, He cannot do otherwise than have mercy on those who lie under such an ailment, and as a gracious **Head**, have pity on them. Now the **Believer** must look out for Him as such **a One**, and go to Him on this ground with confidence and boldness, and lay his case and state open before Him, so that He might help and send deliverance.

**Secondly**, he must also look upon **Christ** as mighty to save from that state, and to command that light shine out of the darkness; and consequently as one who is able to save to the uttermost all who come to **God** through Him, **Heb. 7: v. 25.**

**Firstly**, this is not their case alone; others have been in similar situations before, and many have had similar complaints in all ages, as is known to those who have been familiar with *tried souls* <note>A "tried soul" is a person whose faith has been tested by spiritual hardship, doubt, or the feeling of being abandoned by God.</note>.

**Fourthly**, although the distinct knowledge and comprehension of one’s *state* <note>Referring to one's "state of grace," or the subjective certainty that one is among the saved.</note> is comforting and refreshing, it is not *absolutely* necessary; a soul can be a saved soul even if these clouds should last until the day of its death, and even if they, as long as they lived, never received a clear discovery of their state of grace, but instead spent their days in mourning, complaining, and crying out over darkness, etc.

**Fifthly**, such a soul should reflect that it is a great mercy to be kept out of hell for so long; and certainly, the thoughts of what one is and what one deserves can make the heart moderate, so that one does not count it a small thing, even if one does not reach so high as to see one’s name written in the **Book of Life** <note>A biblical reference to the list of those destined for eternal life (Revelation 20:12).</note>.

**Seventhly**, if they reach any actual ground for hope, however small it may be, they should value it highly; for many who are dear to **Christ** live a long time and do not even know what even that much is.

# How and in what manner. #

1. Whether the voice <note>original: "stemme Christi"</note> of Christ / which makes the dead alive / has been heard and welcomed in their soul / or not? This is the <term>effectual calling: "krachtdadige roeping," the theological concept of God's internal, irresistible call to the soul</term>.
2. Whether there has been wrought in their soul a thoroughgoing change / or not? A change in the whole person / so that everything has become new / 2 Cor. 5: 17.
3. Whether there is a principle of life within them / or not? and whether they are led by the Spirit.
4. Whether there is a life lived unto the glory of the Lord Redeemer / or not.

And when we come through impartial examination to discover the wickedness of our state / should we not then be stirred up / to take heed concerning ourselves / and to labor by all means / to get out of it, considering /

1. How sad and pitiable this state is.
2. How grim and terrible the consequences of it are.
3. How blessed a thing it is / to be delivered from this miserable and sinful state.

->when we are sluggish toward our duties.<-

But if one asks: what can those do for whom the thought of the duty itself—and the very contemplation of it—is a source of terror?

I answer: it may be that some, if not much of this, flows from a certain **bodily imbalance** <term>ongetempertheydt: a lack of "temperament" or physical equilibrium, often referring to a nervous or melancholy state of health</term>, which causes a physical disturbance upon the penetrating realization of something that is weighty and of great importance; so much so that they cannot bear to be deeply affected by anything. But leaving that to others <note>The author likely means leaving the medical diagnosis to physicians.</note>, I would advise such a soul toward these duties:

**First**, that he should frequently set himself to the duty, such as **Prayer**, even if it should stir up the imbalance of his body; for with time that will wear off, or at least diminish. Whereas giving in to it will make the duty more and more terrifying to him, and thus make him even more unfit for it. In doing so, he would perform a pleasing service to Satan, who perhaps also has a hand in that bodily imbalance. When the poor soul is thus accustomed, or has a habit of undertaking the duty, it will finally not seem as terrifying as it used to, and so the body will not be as quickly disturbed by it as it once was.

**Secondly**, if such a person can do no more, he should keep his love for the duty and his desires for the same fresh and lively, and not allow them to wither away entirely.

**Thirdly**, he should be frequent in the use of frequent **brief arrows of prayer** <note>original: "uitschietingen," referring to "ejaculatory prayers"—short, spontaneous prayers sent up to God throughout the day.</note> and short pleadings sent up to God. For these will not make such a heavy impression on the body, and thus will not cause the stirring and awakening of the bodily imbalance, as the more solemn approaches to God in prayer might easily do.

**Fourthly**, if he cannot go to **Christ** with confidence to draw life and strength from him according to his need, he can nonetheless cast a look upon him, even if it were only from afar, and he can think of him,

1. When they cannot come with confidence and draw from Him through faith, which the state of their soul requires; they cannot "draw water with joy from the wells of salvation," <note>original: "Fonteynen des heyls," a reference to Isaiah 12:3</note> but they keep themselves at a distance and give way to suspicious thoughts about Him. This is a step of unbelief, paving the way for more.

2. When they cannot with confidence declare and confess their portion in Him, as the Church did in Isaiah 12:v. 2: *Behold, God is my salvation, I will trust, and not fear: for the Lord Jehovah is my Strength, and Song, and He is become my salvation.*

3. When they must call into doubt whether they have truly laid hold of Christ, and thus cannot go to Him for the fulfillment of their shortcomings and needs.

4. When they, moreover, call into doubt whether it is permitted by God and whether they are free to come to Him and lay hold of Him; indeed, when they believe they have many reasons to maintain this unbelief and to keep themselves from the righteousness of Christ.

5. When, even if they do look to Him, it is with a great mixture of unbelieving fear—that they will be no better for it, or indeed, they doubt whether it will be to their advantage or not.

6. This unbelief will proceed further, and they may come to the point that they not only conclude they have no part or lot in Him, but also conclude that their case is desperate and incurable; and so they say, there is no more hope, they are "cut off" for their part, as in Ezekiel 37:v. 11, and so they lie as if dead and lost.

7. Indeed, they can go further, and utter certain desperate thoughts and expressions about God, to the great offense of the Godly <term>Vroome: the pious or devout believers</term> and the dishonor of God.

8. And still further, they can finally come to call into doubt all the promises, and cry out with David in his haste <note>original: "haaste," referring to a state of sudden alarm, panic, or agitation</note> in Psalm 116:v. 11, *that all men are liars.*

### How to Use Christ as the Life,

9. Yes, they can come to this: that they regard the entire *Gospel* <note>original: "Euangelium"</note> as nothing other than a heap of deceptions and a cleverly devised fable, or merely simple concepts and *Fantasies* <note>original: "Phantasien"</note>.

Secondly, let us see where this originates. The causes of this can be brought under three headings.

Firstly, the Holy *God* has a holy hand in this, and He has noble ends and purposes before Him in this matter; such as:

1. The Lord may think it good to arrange things thus, so that He might magnify His power and grace in rescuing those who were turned toward the mouth of hell, and who seemed to many to be lost and perished, without any possibility of recovery.

2. So that He—in thus punishing them for giving in to the first movements of unbelief—might warn everyone to guard against such evil, and not to cherish or give in to groundless complaints, nor to entertain the objections made against their spiritual state by the *Devil*.

3. So that He warns everyone to walk carefully, and to work out their salvation with fear and trembling <note>A reference to the biblical exhortation in Philippians 2:12</note>, not knowing what might come upon them before they die.

4. So that He teaches everyone to walk humbly, as those who do not know what advantage *Satan* might get over them before all is finished; and to see how they have need of *Christ* daily to strengthen their faith, and to hold fast their grip on Him.

5. The Lord may think it good to deal thus with some, so that He might give a full proof of His great forbearance <note>original: "verdraagzaamheydt"</note> and longsuffering <note>original: "langmoedigheydt"</note> in bearing with such people, and for so long.

1. **Pride** and **haughtiness** of the heart, thinking that their mountain stands so firm that it cannot be moved; and this provokes God to hide His face, as in **Psalm 30** <note>The author refers to Psalm 30:6-7: "In my prosperity I said, I shall never be moved... **Thirdly**, They must be thoroughly convinced of the **treachery**, **deceitfulness**, and **godlessness** of their own heart, so that they may see it is not worthy of being trusted. ## CHAPTER XXV.

### How Christ is to be used as the Life, by one who is so dead and unfeeling that they cannot know what to judge of themselves, or of their own state, other than that it is of no worth.

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial "W" featuring ornate foliate and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc> We have indeed spoken something of this same case when we spoke of **Christ** as the **Truth**; yet we shall speak a little of it here. However, we shall not expand upon the particulars mentioned before, and therefore we shall speak a little of these five specific things:

1. I shall show what this spiritual disorder <term>ongestalte</term> <note>The original Dutch term "ongestalte" refers to a state of spiritual "misshapenness" or malaise where a person feels out of sorts or deformed in their religious life.</note> is.
2. From where it arises, and how the **Soul** comes to fall into it.
3. How **Christ**, as the **Life**, brings about a restoration from it.
4. How the **Soul** must exercise itself so that it may obtain a restoration.
5. I shall answer some Questions or Objections.

As for the first: **Believers** can sometimes be so dead that they not only cannot see that they have a part in **Christ**, and are uncertain what to judge of themselves, but they are also so carried away with prejudices and misconceptions that they will judge nothing of themselves but that their state is of no worth; indeed, they will not only deny and mislabel the good that **God** has wrought in them by His **Spirit**, but will also argue that they are outside the state of **Grace**, and

This arises (which is the second part) partly from **God**’s hiding of His face and the changing of His dealings with them, surrounding them with clouds; and partly from themselves and their own misconceptions, such as:

1. Because they judge their state not by the unchangeable rule of the truth, but by the outward dealings of **God**, which change even toward the best of people.

2. Because they judge their state by the observable measure of **Grace** within them; and thus they conclude that their condition is poor because they notice that corruption gains the upper hand from time to time, while **Grace** seems to diminish. They perceive no victory over temptations, nor any growth in **Grace**, etc.

3. Because they judge their state by comparison with others; thus they imagine they cannot be **Believers** because they are so unlike those whom they consider to be true **Believers**. This is also judging by a wrong standard.

4. Because they judge themselves by their former selves; that is, because they seem so different from what they once were, they conclude that their state cannot be good. This, too, is a wrong standard by which to judge one’s condition.

5. Because they begin to test and examine their case and condition but do not reach a conclusion or result; so when they have finished, they are just as much in the dark and uncertain about how to judge themselves as when they began. Or,

6. Because they make little or no effort to earnestly test themselves as if before the face of **God**, but rest content with a superficial examination <note>original: "overloopse beproevingh" — a cursory or "running-over" look rather than a deep, heart-searching inquiry.</note> that can lead to no good result.

But one will say (and so I come to the final part): suppose that after all this I remain as I was before—just as incapable of rightly judging my state <note>original: "staat" — refers to one’s spiritual status or standing before God, i.e., whether one is truly converted or not.</note> as ever?

I answer: **Nevertheless**, you must persevere in laying hold of Christ, in loving him, in looking toward him, and in casting a lost, dead soul with all your needs upon him; and you must take this to heart as your constant work. Indeed, you must strive to grow in these direct acts of Faith <note>The "direct acts of faith" (*actus directus*) involve the soul looking directly at Christ for salvation, while "reflexive acts" (*actus reflexus*) involve the soul looking inward to see if it truly believes. The author argues the former is more essential than the latter.</note> and learn to submit yourself to God in this, knowing that those reflexive acts of faith are not absolutely necessary; indeed, you should value it highly if he finally brings you to Heaven, even if you were covered by a cloud all your days.

But others (you say) receive more clarity.

I answer: **I grant that; yet know this**, that not everyone receives clarity, and those who have it do not have it in the same measure. And must God give you as much as he gives to someone else? Suppose you could not make the proper use of it that others do, but instead you became proud because of it and forgot yourself? **Therefore**, it will be best to give God the freedom to distribute his tokens of favor <note>original: "gunst-bewijsen"</note> according to his will, and for you to occupy yourself with your commanded duties: the exercise of faith, love, fear, patience, etc.

But, if I could at any time get a glimpse of my state, it would be some peace and contentment to me.

I answer: **That** I grant; and how do you know whether you might receive that favor before you die? **Why**, then, will you not wait until it is convenient for him?

But in the meantime, the lack of it makes me go heartless and discouraged to my commanded duties, and it means I cannot distinctively apply matters to myself.

I answer: **Nevertheless**, the command is the same, the offer is the same, and the encouragement is the same. Why then should you not go forward and lean on Christ in the Wilderness <note>A reference to Song of Solomon 8:5: "Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved?" In this context, the "wilderness" represents a period of spiritual trial and lack of sensible comfort.</note>, even if you lack that consoling light?

But, it **is something else** to have a clear sight of my

# How to use Christ as the Life,

to miss [assurance of my] state / and to judge otherwise of myself / that I am still in the state of nature <note>original: "staat der natuure" — a theological term referring to the spiritual condition of a person before they have experienced conversion or "the state of grace."</note> / and that is my case.

Furthermore, I would add these few things to it.

First, take no pleasure / in disputing against your own soul: for that is only to serve the purpose of **Satan**.

Secondly, be not too hasty / or too ready / to drink in prejudices against the work of **God** in your own souls; for that is to conspire with **Satan** against your souls.

Thirdly, value greatly a little light / that he is pleased to give to you / even if it were but of one mark <note>original: "markteken" — a "mark" or sign of grace used by believers to identify if they are truly born again.</note> / and do not be hard to please: for a scriptural mark / as for example / love for the Brothers <note>The author refers to 1 John 3:14: "We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brothers." But enough of this case here.

# CHAPTER XXVII.

## Seventhly, How shall one use Christ as the Life when struggling with an angry God because of sin?

<image-desc>Large ornamental drop cap 'O' featuring intricate floral and scrollwork designs within a square border.</image-desc>
In order that we may give some satisfaction to this question, we shall:

1. Show what the ingredients are in this case, or what typically comes together in this <term>state of distress</term> <note>The original Dutch 'ongestalte' refers to a spiritual condition of being 'out of shape' or in a state of spiritual ailment and disorder.</note>.
2. We shall point out some reasons why it pleases the Lord to deal thus with His people.
3. We shall show how Christ is the Life for the soul in this case.
4. We shall point out the duty of the believer toward restoration. And
5. Add a word or two of warning.

As for the first matter: there may be these parts, or ingredients, in this state of distress:

1. That God sets their sins before their eyes, so that they will cry out, *Our sin is ever before us*, Psalm 51: verse 5, and say, as it is written in Psalm 90: verse 8: *You set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your countenance*; and so He can make them see that the Lord contends over sin, just as the Church did in Isaiah 59: verses 11, 12, 13. *We all roar* <note>original: "brommen"; likely referring to the mourning or moaning like bears mentioned in Isaiah 59:11.</note>...

9. What is even more terrifying: He can write their sin upon their judgment, just as when He caused the sword and adultery to follow **David’s House**. <note>This refers to the biblical narrative where, as a consequence of David's sin with Bathsheba, his own family was plagued by violence and sexual scandal (2 Samuel 12).</note>

10. And finally, He can cause them to fear being cast away entirely, as in **Psalm 51 verse 13**. 

> *Cast me not away from your presence,* he said.

And the **Lord** sees fit to do this (to say a word regarding the second chapter) for these and similar reasons:

1. So that He may reveal to them and to all the **World** how righteous, **Holy**, and just a **God** He is, who cannot approve of or tolerate sin, even in His own children.

2. So that He may cause all to fear and tremble before this great and **Holy God**, who is awesome in His judgments, even when they come from a Father’s hand—one who does not pursue in mere wrath and fury, but chastens in love. Surely all must consider that His dealings with the **Godless** shall be far more fearful and terrifying, since they are not yet reconciled to Him through the blood of **Christ**.

3. So that He might drive them more earnestly toward **Christ**, so that they might receive a new <term>extract</term> <note>In this 17th-century context, an 'extract' refers to a fresh copy or a formal renewal of a legal document—here, the subjective assurance of God's pardon.</note> of their **Pardon**, and that their souls may be washed in the **Blood of Jesus**.

4. So that He may teach them to walk more cautiously thereafter, and to guard themselves more carefully against **Satan’s** temptations, and to make greater use of **Christ** as their strength, light, and **Guide**.

5. So that He may cause them to see their great obligation to **Jesus Christ**, because He has delivered them from that state of wrath in which they were by nature just like others, and in which they would have remained for all eternity had He not delivered them.

6. So that He may exercise their faith, patience, and hope, and see whether they will believe in hope against hope, and take hold of the strength of the **Lord**, so that they might make peace with Him, **Isaiah 27 verse 5**.

### How to use Christ as the Life

7. So that He may give a fresh proof of His wonderful mercy, grace, love, and compassion—upholding the soul in the meantime, and finally forgiving her and speaking peace to their souls through the **Blood of Jesus**.

But as for the third chapter, we may look upon **Christ** as the **Life** in this case, based on these grounds:

**Firstly**, He has satisfied justice and thus bore the pure wrath of **God** which was deserved by their sins; He has trodden the winepress alone, **Isaiah 63:3**. He was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our sins, **Isaiah 53:5, 10**; and therefore they <note>That is, the believers.</note> do not drink from this cup <note>referring to the 'cup of God's fury'.</note> which would make them drunk and cause them to stagger and fall, never to rise again.

**Secondly**, He has also brought it about that mercy and love shall accompany all those sharp dealings, and that these shall bloom out of mercy; yes, even that they shall be as a **Covenant-blessing**, promised in the **Covenant**, **Psalm 89:31, 34**.

**Thirdly**, the **Lord Jesus** is pleased at times to let them see this clear distinction between the blows under which they lie and the judgments of pure wrath intended for the **Godless**; and this sustains the soul: for then she sees that those dealings, however sharp they may be, shall work together for her good and come from the hand of a gracious and loving Father, reconciled in the blood of **Christ**.

**Fourthly**, He is a **Prince**, exalted to give to **Israel** repentance and forgiveness of sins, **Acts 5:31**. Indeed, He has secured such a clause in the **Covenant**—which is in all things well-ordered and sure—that upon their renewal of faith and repentance, their <term>later sins</term> <note>The original Dutch 'na-sonden' refers specifically to sins committed by a believer after their initial conversion or 'justification'.</note> shall be forgiven. And besides the promises of faith and repentance in the **Covenant**, this also provides assurance that they shall receive both: namely, that He is a **Prince**, exalted to give both.

# The Translator's Warning.

take care / that you do not, instead of drawing an **Evangelical** holiness <note>original: "Euangelische heyligheidt"; holiness based on the Gospel of grace rather than adherence to the Law</note> from **Christ** / content yourself with a natural **Socinian Morality** <term>Socinianism: A rationalist theological movement that denied the divinity of Jesus and viewed religion primarily as a system of ethical conduct rather than spiritual rebirth.</term> / from which **Rebirth** <note>original: "Wedergeboorte"</note> and the **Spirit of Christ** are far removed. Thirdly, that you guard yourself / against being led away from the **Evangelical** way of working by the preaching of many Teachers: for it is all too evident / that very many Teachers in the **Netherlands** / however much they wish to uphold the **Reformed Doctrine** regarding the grace of **Christ**, in fact preach the **Gospel** and **Holiness** in a **Legalistic** <note>original: "Wettisch"; focusing on rules, duties, and human effort rather than the internal work of grace.</note> manner / so that they point people toward duties with motives and means / without showing them / how to make use of **Christ** for that purpose through faith: Indeed, many grasp faith so poorly / that they think / its nature consists in an assurance / and firm confidence / that **God** is reconciled with us for **Christ’s** sake / and that **He** is our **Savior** / who died for us: whereby the poor people are terribly misled and deceived / thinking / they must only firmly imagine / and hold it to be true / that **Christ** has paid for their sins / and that **He** will take them to **Heaven** when they die / and that is all the faith / that they know: not understanding / much less practicing the going out toward the **Lord Jesus** / and the laying hold of him for righteousness / and strength / in which faith and the life of faith consist: whereby they also do not know how to draw any sanctifying grace from **Christ** / and therefore continue to live in sins / and perish. If they were teachable / I would trust / that this little book / and these addresses would be singularly useful to them. Yet may the **Lord** give to them and to you understanding and discernment in this. The grace of **Jesus** be with you. **Amen**.

-># Regarding the free and full grace of Christ <note>original: *Christi*</note> #<-

If we perceived how grace has arranged everything for our best, and most for the honor and exaltation of its own grace, we would sit down and sing under God's saddest dealings with us; and living by faith and hope, we would rejoice in the full expectation of a gracious outcome. For as long as grace reigns (and that shall be until glory takes over the dominion), everything shall flow in the channel of grace; and although feeling <note>In 17th-century theology, "feeling" (subjective emotion) was often viewed as a "false friend" because it fluctuates, unlike the steady "faith" in God's promises.</note> (which is often an unfaithful friend of faith) is always giving a false report of His grace to unbelief—and thereby stirring up discontents, doubts, fears, jealousies, and many disturbances in the soul to its own detriment and damage—yet grace shall in the end be seen to be grace. And believers will receive such a full view of this manifold grace—as it arranges, tempers, orders, shortens, or lengthens all the sad and dreary days and times that have passed over their heads, or over their mother's head <note>Likely referring to the Church, often described as the "Mother" of the faithful.</note>; they shall see that grace arranged everything, even to every circumstance of all the various struggles and changes—the ups and downs—that came upon them.

And oh, what a satisfying sight that will be, when the general assembly and church of the firstborn <note>original: *generaale Vergadering en Gemeinte der Eerst-geboorne*; a reference to Hebrews 12:23.</note> who are written in heaven, and all the individual saints shall come and take a view of all their experiences! The summary of which shall be: grace began, grace advanced, and grace perfected everything; grace was at the foundation of everything, and grace crowned everything. What shouts there shall be: "Grace, grace be unto it!" when the headstone <note>original: *Hooft-steen*; refers to Zechariah 4:7, where the finishing of the Temple is greeted with shouts of "Grace!"</note> shall be brought forth! What a looking back upon the same shall give a soul-satisfying pleasure and wonder over it! When everyone shall have to say: grace has done everything well; not the least of all the work of grace in and about me should have been missing; now I see that the work of God is perfect; grace was glorious grace, and wise grace, whatever I thought of it;

-># Author’s Address #<-

Oh, what a fool I have been in my murmuring, and in not being fully satisfied with all that grace did with me. But enough of this for now.

Let me now draw a little closer, Christian Reader, to the occasion and objectives of writing and publishing this present treatise. It is evident to all who do not willfully wish to close their eyes that there is now, and long has been, among the Professing Believers <note>original: *Belijders*; those who publicly profess their faith, particularly within the Reformed tradition.</note> of the Truth a wicked abuse of God’s mercy and goodness, offered and presented to us in the mystery of the Gospel of God's grace. In this Gospel, the exceeding riches of His grace are shown to us through His kindness toward us in Christ Jesus. Yet, our blemishes are not the blemishes of God’s children <note>A biblical allusion suggesting that the sins of the people are not those of the truly redeemed, but of those who are unfaithful.</note>; no fruits are seen, even among the most prominent Believers, that correspond with the labor and effort the Lord has expended on us.

There is not that Evangelical holiness, tenderness, watchfulness, growth in grace and in the knowledge of Jesus Christ—that growing up into Christ in all things—that heavenly-mindedness, that fellowship with the Father and with His Son Jesus Christ, and that walk in Heaven which the ministry of grace, under which we have long lived, demands from our hands. Alas, our grapes are wild and foul-smelling; therefore the Lord seems ready to contend with us. He has already given over many—who would not receive the love of the truth so that they might be saved—to a spirit of error, so that they might believe the lie. And He puts many others in danger of being drawn away into crooked paths by men of corrupt minds, who have been and still are busy boldly spreading damnable doctrines, to the perversion of the doctrine of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, and to the overthrowing of even the foundations of our hope and assurance. 

In particular, Satan has recently for this purpose used the <term>Quakers</term> <note>A radical religious group that emerged in 17th-century England, often criticized by contemporary theologians for their emphasis on the "Inner Light" over traditional Church structure and Scripture.</note> in England, and—what I am also chiefly focusing on now—certain people called <term>Moralists</term> <note>original: *Moralisten*; philosophers or teachers who emphasize human ethics and "good works" over the necessity of divine grace and spiritual rebirth.</note> or <term>Moral-writers</term>...

### Regarding the free and full grace of Christ. ###

**Christians**, I thought / that a treatise on such a sub- ject / which I deemed very necessary at all times / and espe- cially in such a day of danger / must be formed ac- cording to the understanding of both the one and the other; the most wise can receive good through that which is suited to the understanding of children; whereas these <note>The "children," or those simple in faith.</note> can draw little edification / from that which is suited to the mouth of those; and the less experienced / or those of smaller understanding are less capable / of bringing a general piece down to particulars; the bread must be cut small for them / or they will receive little profit from it <note>original: *het broodt moet haar kleyn gesneden worden*; a common 17th-century metaphor for breaking down complex theological concepts into simple, digestible instructions.</note>; and I trust that the wise will notice some smaller or larger vari- ety / even where the particulars seem at first sight very unnecessarily multi- plied.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the believer’s complete devotion to Christ. ### Concerning Evangelical Holiness.

While others seek their own, it is his—only his, his one and his all—to seek that which is Christ’s, that blessed Seeker who came to seek him and to save him; and having been found by Him, he strives to conduct himself as one who is no longer his own. The glorification of Him in his body and Spirit, which are His, as having been bought by Him, is his heaven begun; and the greatest work that he has to do in Heaven is to obtain a clearer vision of that blessed object of all wonder and adoration, and to be in a better state to praise Him for eternity.

Now this is but a short and general sketch, drawn by an unskilled hand, of that holiness which shall stand the tests, and which shall be found true when it is tested against the **Touchstone of the Word** <note>The "Touchstone of the Word" refers to using the Bible as the ultimate standard to test the purity of religious doctrine, much as a touchstone was used to test the purity of gold.</note>.

But let us, on the other hand, briefly consider what our **Moralists** <term>Moralists (Moralisten) — MacWard is likely criticizing the "Latitudinarians" or "Neonomians" of the 17th century, who emphasized ethics and natural law over the necessity of supernatural grace.</term> put in its place, as being in their estimation more beautiful to the eye and more useful for the souls of men; They make a great fuss over holiness; yet the cause for which they plead, and toward which they wish to move people, is a kind of holiness derived from natural abilities, in which Christ, the Spirit, and the Gospel of God's grace are allowed no other part nor more powerful assistance than to cooperate by way of command, motives, and example; This is now in England that admired and applauded **Diana** <note>A reference to Acts 19:28, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians." The author uses this to suggest that "Morality" has become a pagan idol that people worship in place of true Christianity.</note>, *Morality*; it is true, sometimes they mutter through their teeth a lukewarm acknowledgement that the Gospel gives men some special help, and is of singular use and benefit in showing the way and rule with greater clarity, and directing how to walk clearly therein, and awakening us by noble examples; and some add to it some feeble and cold movements of the Holy Spirit, sent out in the distribution of this truth to make men more awake in the work; but all this, **saving the right** <note>original: "salvo jure" — a Latin legal phrase meaning "without prejudice to the right." MacWard uses it sarcastically to suggest these thinkers only accept God's help as long as it doesn't infringe on their own perceived natural autonomy.</note>

Bb 2
<meta>catchword: of</meta>

<summary>MacWard defines true holiness as being entirely centered on Christ's ownership of the believer, contrasting it with the "Morality" of his day, which he argues relies too heavily on human nature and treats the Holy Spirit as a mere assistant.</summary>

# Address of Mr. Macward,

...of the great *Diana* <note>original: "Diana"; a reference to the pagan goddess of Ephesus in Acts 19:28, often used by Reformed theologians to symbolize a man-made idol—in this case, the idol of human free will and self-righteousness.</note>; so much and no more is granted to the *Gospel* than that it clearly shows men how they might release and exercise their own innate strength; it gives them some particular help in holding, or rather snuffing, the candle <note>To "snuff" a candle in the 17th century meant to trim the burnt part of the wick so the flame would burn more brightly and clearly.</note>, so that they may see with more dignity how to work, and so that through the motives and examples it brings forward, they might have a singular awakening to the practice of these commanded virtues; the *Gospel*, with all that it brings and does, does no more than hold the candle until these craftsmen weave their web and form and display their garment, and then it lets them see how they put it on, and once put on, it lets them be moved to wear it as the highest beauty and the principal ornament of the soul; this is all the *provision* they lay up for eternity, and in this attire of gilded *Morality* <term>Gilded Morality (vergulde Moraliteyt) — something that appears precious like gold on the outside but is made of base metal within; a critique of outward ethics lacking spiritual substance.</term> they intend to approach God and appear before His Judgment Seat with the confidence that they shall be accepted; they wish to pay their own way to Heaven and carry a sum of money with them to purchase the inheritance of the saints in light, with a small discount which a mercy of their own making (for it is not God’s mercy) must provide, and thus they make everything certain.

They heap up words about virtue, the love of God, *mortification* <term>Mortification — the spiritual practice of "putting to death" the sinful nature or worldly desires.</term>, etc.; but they have truly taken away our Lord *Jesus Christ*, and they will not tell us where they have laid Him <note>A reference to Mary Magdalene’s words at the empty tomb in John 20:13, used here to suggest that the "Moralists" have removed Christ from the center of the faith.</note>, for fear that we should go seeking Him and leave them; what are these rotten, loathsome rags wherewith they clothe us so that the shame of our nakedness might not be seen, compared to that holiness to which we were foreordained before the foundation of the world; and to which we (to the end that we might obtain the salvation and glory of the Lord *Jesus Christ*, whereunto...
